title: Immunoinformatics-based design of a multi-epitope mRNA vaccine candidate targeting the major human-infecting hepatitis E virus genotypes 1-4.
authors: Khonza, Maham Mehrangaze; Saeed, Zain; Jabeen, Zohra; Arab, Wafaa; Kakakhel, Sehrish; Yamin, Maham; Ghaith, Mazen M; Javed, Aneela; Zohaib, Ali; Abdulal, Rwaa H
one_liner_zh: 该文是免疫信息学设计针对戊型肝炎病毒的多表位mRNA疫苗，涉及分子模拟但对象为病毒疫苗，与染色质三维组织及基因组调控建模无关，无可迁移启发。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is one of the leading causes of acute and chronic hepatitis among humans across the globe and is linked to severe diseases in immunocompromised individuals and pregnant women. Despite its substantial global burden, only one vaccine is licensed (in China and Pakistan), limiting its global accessibility. Furthermore, no globally approved mRNA vaccine against HEV is currently available, highlighting the need to develop strategies for alternative vaccines. METHODS: In this study, the amino acid sequences of ORF2 capsid proteins representative of HEV genotypes 1-4 were curated, retrieved, and analyzed to generate a consensus sequence. The conserved cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL), helper T lymphocyte (HTL), and B-cell epitopes were computationally screened based on their antigenicity, allergenicity, toxicity, IFN-gamma induction, and human non-homology. Then, the selected epitopes, seven in total, were assembled into a computational multi-epitope mRNA construct incorporated with beta-defensin adjuvant, correct linkers, and regulatory elements [Kozak, tPA, MITD, and globin untranslated regions (UTRs)]. The construct was subsequently subjected to structural modeling, refinement and validation, docked with the TLR1/TLR2 heterodimer, followed by normal mode analysis and a 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation with MM-GBSA binding free-energy estimation, immune simulations, codon optimization, and in silico vaccine construct design. RESULTS: The computational analyses predicted that the proposed epitopes possessed a favorable antigenicity (VaxiJen score >/=0.4-1), with non-allergenicity and epitope conservancy (80%-100%) across the analyzed HEV genotypes (1-4), and that the assembled vaccine construct was structurally stable. Protein-protein docking of the vaccine construct candidate with the TLR1/TLR2 heterodimer and normal mode analysis of the docked complex indicated a stable structural interface rather than a confirmation of biological receptor engagement; a subsequent 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation supported a persistent, increasingly hydrogen-bonded interface with a favorable MM-GBSA binding free-energy (-91.96 kcal/mol). Computational immune simulations predicted cellular and humoral immune responses with B- and T-cell interaction activity and cytokine production levels. CONCLUSION: This study describes a computationally designed multi-epitope mRNA vaccine candidate with predicted immunogenicity and structural stability against the major human-infecting HEV genotypes 1-4. These computational results support the proposed vaccine construct as a promising candidate for further research to assess its immunogenicity; safety and protective efficacy will require experimental validation before its translational potential is verified.
abstract_zh: 背景：戊型肝炎病毒（HEV）是全球人类急性和慢性肝炎的主要病因之一，并与免疫功能低下个体和孕妇中的严重疾病相关。尽管其全球负担重大，目前仅有一种疫苗获得许可（在中国和巴基斯坦），限制了其全球可及性。此外，目前尚无全球批准的针对HEV的mRNA疫苗，凸显了开发替代疫苗策略的必要性。方法：在本研究中，选取、检索并分析了代表HEV基因型1-4的ORF2衣壳蛋白氨基酸序列，以生成共有序列。基于抗原性、致敏性、毒性、IFN-γ诱导性和人类非同源性，对保守的细胞毒性T淋巴细胞（CTL）、辅助性T淋巴细胞（HTL）和B细胞表位进行了计算筛选。随后，将选定的表位（共七个）组装成一个计算性多表位mRNA构建体，并整合了β-防御素佐剂、正确的连接子和调控元件[Kozak、tPA、MITD和珠蛋白非翻译区（UTRs）]。该构建体随后进行了结构建模、优化和验证，与TLR1/TLR2异二聚体进行对接，随后进行正态模式分析和100纳秒分子动力学模拟，并估算MM-GBSA结合自由能、免疫模拟、密码子优化和计算机疫苗构建体设计。结果：计算分析预测，所提出的表位具有良好的抗原性（VaxiJen评分≥0.4-1），具有非致敏性，并在所分析的HEV基因型（1-4）中表现出表位保守性（80%-100%），且组装的疫苗构建体结构稳定。疫苗构建体候选物与TLR1/TLR2异二聚体的蛋白-蛋白对接及对接复合物的正态模式分析表明，结构界面稳定，而非确认生物受体结合；随后的100纳秒分子动力学模拟支持一个持续且氢键增强的界面，并具有有利的MM-GBSA结合自由能（-91.96 kcal/mol）。计算免疫模拟预测了细胞和体液免疫反应，包括B细胞和T细胞相互作用活性及细胞因子产生水平。结论：本研究描述了一个计算设计的针对主要感染人类的HEV基因型1-4的多表位mRNA疫苗候选物，具有预测的免疫原性和结构稳定性。这些计算结果支持所提出的疫苗构建体作为进一步研究其免疫原性的有前景候选物；其安全性和保护效力需在转化潜力验证前通过实验验证。
